title: Talks open in Abu Dhabi, Trump calls the Iran war 'effectively over', and three carriers converge
summary: Russia and Ukraine hold their first US-mediated talks since February, Trump says the Iran war is effectively over militarily while the blockade stays, Hegseth rejects an impeachment push, Hormuz traffic runs far below normal, strikes hit Sanaa, and the Theodore Roosevelt heads west from Singapore as the Makin Island group moves into the Sea of Japan.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Welcome to the ForceFinder Daily Briefing. I'm Avery.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And I'm Cole. As always, this show is generated automatically from the open-source reporting behind the ForceFinder map. Every story has source links on the globe, so treat us as a guide, not the final word.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: It's Tuesday, November tenth. And for the first time since February, Russian and Ukrainian negotiators sat down together, with the United States mediating, in Abu Dhabi.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: The first day ran nearly four hours, and they're due back on Wednesday. Zelensky, after his team briefed him, called it constructive and quite substantive.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the talks very productive. And he said Europeans should be brought to the table. That's notable, because yesterday the Kremlin said Europeans would not take part.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Right. So the question of who's in the room hasn't gone away. Russia's delegation is led again by Vladimir Medinsky.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And the fighting didn't pause for the talks. Overnight, Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched one Iskander ballistic missile and a hundred and sixty-two drones.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: There's also more on Ukraine's strike on the Kirishi refinery, Russia's second-largest, near Saint Petersburg. Euronews reports three of its main processing units were damaged. That hasn't been independently confirmed.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Russia's defence ministry says it intercepted four hundred and thirty Ukrainian drones over Russia and Crimea that night. And the regional governor says one woman was killed by falling debris.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: On the front line, a quieter picture. The Institute for the Study of War assessed that neither side advanced on Monday.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: But it says Russia is relying more on fast, maneuverable missiles that fly like cruise missiles, and on adapted ballistic missiles, to hit Ukrainian infrastructure. That's against the backdrop of the grid attacks we've covered all week.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Now to Iran, where the tone shifted. After meeting Qatar's prime minister on Monday, President Trump said the war is effectively over, militarily.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: He said new strikes were unlikely. But the naval blockade stays in place, along with the new Iron Gate task force going after Iran's land routes.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And Iranian officials dismissed his remarks as fake news. Their demands still include lifting the blockade before anything else moves.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So Washington is talking about the war winding down, but the core standoff over the blockade hasn't changed.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: In Washington today, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth held his first Pentagon news conference in six months. He called an impeachment resolution from Congressman Thomas Massie a political spectacle.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: That resolution accuses him of launching the Iran war without approval from Congress.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Out at sea, the British maritime agency UKMTO put some numbers on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. It describes traffic as below normal, but not stalled.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Its weekly report counted a hundred and seventy outbound and a hundred and fifty-five inbound transits. That's about sixty-five percent below levels before the war. And most ships broadcasting their position are using the northern route, close to Iran.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Central Command says that since July, the blockade has turned back a hundred and forty-seven ships and disabled five. One of those was the bulk carrier Huda, which we covered on Sunday.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And the incidents around the strait haven't stopped. On Saturday night, a tanker caught fire off Khasab, in Oman, and its crew abandoned ship. Open-source analysts have tentatively named it as the Navig8 Messi, but that isn't confirmed.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards blamed mines on unauthorized routes. The British agency still hasn't confirmed what caused any of those fires.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Let's go to Yemen. Residents and the Houthis say overnight strikes in Sanaa hit a gas station and an oil facility. At least one person was killed and nine were wounded.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And the Houthi-run health ministry says Saudi strikes in an area east of Sanaa killed forty-four people, including more than twenty children. Saudi Arabia hasn't confirmed those strikes, and the toll hasn't been verified.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: This all follows the weekend missile attack on Riyadh that damaged an Aramco building. Both sides say they're responding to the other.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: In Gaza, Palestinian reports cited by Haaretz say three people, including a child, were killed and sixteen wounded in Israeli strikes over the past day. Drop Site reported an airstrike on a shelter in the Zeitoun neighbourhood of Gaza City killed two. The counts differ between sources.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And in southern Lebanon, Drop Site, citing Al Jazeera and Lebanon's state news agency, reported Israeli jets struck the town of Qantara, and Israeli forces fired toward the outskirts of Chaqra. No casualty figures were reported.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: In Sudan, the local outlet Darfur24 reported drone strikes by both the army and the Rapid Support Forces across Blue Nile, the Kordofan states and North Darfur last week.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: It says the toll from a Rapid Support Forces strike on a fuel station in Taqali al-Abbasiya, in South Kordofan, rose to more than nineteen civilians. And a drone killed at least two people in Damazin.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Now the ships, because there's real movement this week. The new USNI fleet tracker came out on Monday.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: It confirms the George Washington and the George H. W. Bush are both in the Arabian Sea, supporting operations against Iran. The George Washington has been in the region since August nineteenth.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And the Theodore Roosevelt has left Singapore, heading west toward the Gulf, according to Maritime Executive and Misbar. It's expected to relieve the George Washington. A US official told Axios it won't enter Central Command's area before mid-November.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Which means, for a while at least, there could be three US carriers in the region at once.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And one more. The amphibious assault ship Makin Island left Yokosuka, in Japan, on Saturday, according to ship spotters cited by USNI. Its group, with Marines from the Thirteenth Marine Expeditionary Unit, is now in the Sea of Japan.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Fox News has reported, citing US officials, that the group is ultimately bound for the Middle East. We'll keep following it.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: So, what to watch. Day two in Abu Dhabi, and whether Europeans join. Whether Trump's 'effectively over' talk turns into actual negotiations with Iran. And the Roosevelt's arrival in the Arabian Sea.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: That's the briefing. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you tomorrow.
